competitive_landscape: The lake is served today by a state slow ro-pax service and local wooden longboats. The pain is slow crossings, infrequent sailings and basic, ageing vessels on a flagship destination that the government is otherwise investing heavily to modernise. Foiling shuttles complement the vehicle ferries (which carry cars) by adding a fast, comfortable passenger tier — partnership, not displacement.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: This is a textbook all-electric market. Every route is ≤30 nm, the water is sheltered freshwater (no salt corrosion, lower lifecycle cost), and the mainland terminals at Parapat, Ajibata, Tomok and Pangururan are being purpose-built now — so charging can be designed in before commissioning. All-electric is structurally the dominant and sufficient platform here.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not required: the entire operating envelope is bounded by the caldera, with no leg beyond ~30 nm and no salt-water line-haul. The long-range hybrid has no application on the lake — this is a single-platform, all-electric destination.

precedents.what: ~100-vessel, $100M phased clean-marine network with JIH Global, first 5 vessels in 2026
precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a government-aligned clean-marine network being financed and built into a flagship water destination — the model for spec-ing foiling shuttles into a super-priority destination's purpose-built terminals.

regulatory_note: Operations run under a freshwater inland-water class regime (distinct from coastal sea-transport certification) and the lake-port authority, with the Toba Lake Authority (BPODT) coordinating the federal super-priority infrastructure programme. A single authority spanning the purpose-built terminal portfolio plus the UNESCO Geopark conservation mandate gives a clean, low-emission, quiet-mode service a strong design-in pathway.
seasonality: Equatorial freshwater lake with no monsoon hard-closure and no typhoon exposure. The main variable is afternoon downslope (katabatic) wind off the caldera rim, 15–25 kt, which can kick up short chop on the longer mid-lake crossings; sheltered embayments stay calm and foiling rides above the chop. Occasional volcanic ashfall from nearby Sinabung is managed around weather-agency advisories.

summary: Lake Toba is a ~100 km caldera lake in North Sumatra and one of Indonesia's five federal super-priority tourist destinations, with Samosir Island at its heart. More than a million domestic visitors a year reach Samosir by slow ro-pax from Parapat — a 6 km crossing that takes ~45 minutes today. Every meaningful route is short (≤30 nm), the water is calm freshwater (no salt corrosion), and the lake's mainland terminals are being purpose-built with central-government infrastructure money right now. It is close to an ideal all-electric operating environment, and the chance to design clean, fast, quiet shuttles into a flagship destination's transport is open today.
tagline: The world's largest volcanic crater lake — over a million visitors a year, still crossing it on slow ferries.

use_cases.body: Replace the ~45-minute Parapat↔Tomok/Tuktuk slow ro-pax with a ~10-minute all-electric foiling shuttle — the visible 'world-class transport' upgrade for a federal super-priority destination, calm freshwater and short hops making it a clean fit for all-electric.
